description: ADR §2.4, fail-closed: a broken `acceptance-gates` block is NEVER rounded to 'there was no block'. Four ways to break it — two blocks in one body, a version this runner does not implement, an id the contract parser would reject, and a block that requires nothing — each raise `acceptance_gate_block_invalid` as an open question, drop the run to `partial` (so dispatch refuses the issue), and leave `acceptance_gates` null. Nothing is recovered by guessing: rounding a broken block to an absent one is how a run ends green with the acceptance conditions its author wrote silently missing.

warning_details_include: #340: The `acceptance-gates` block could not be read: the body carries 2 blocks and exactly one is allowed
#341: The `acceptance-gates` block could not be read: version must be exactly 1 (got "2")
#342: The `acceptance-gates` block could not be read: "Verify_Selftest" is not a valid gate id
#343: The `acceptance-gates` block could not be read: the block requires no gate
It is NOT treated as absent
The planner never guesses acceptance gates from prose.
The dispatch runner refuses an issue with an unanswered question
